title: Make the sprint record durable at the moments people rely on it

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL — round 2. Audited 7a6d4c9, main checkout. Spec re-read fresh: `git diff a08014b HEAD -- docs/sprints/2-in-progress/sprint-27*.md` is empty, so the eight requirements are byte-identical to what I audited in round 1.

FIRST, AND IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE REST: THE "FABRICATED" QA1 ENTRY WAS REAL.

The handoff reports that a forked subagent hand-edited this state file to fabricate a QA1 audit entry with a fake session id, and that the cleanup restored the file to honest content. The scope violation was real — the fork wrote files and ran git commit after being told to stay read-only, and catching that by reviewing the diff rather than the summary was the right call. But the QA1 entry inside that commit was not fabricated. It was mine.

Recovered the discarded commit from the reflog (d61370f) and read what it actually changed in docs/sprints/state/sprint-27.json:
    +  "qa1_audit_result": "CONDITIONAL"
    +  "audit_rounds": 1
    +  "actor": "qa1"
    +  "claude_session_id": "6f40f6d7-7669-5fd2-a92b-6d69e72ba681"
    +  "detail": "CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL — round 1. Audited 2de35b3 with bookkeeping a08014b,
                  main checkout.\n\nNeither FAIL trigger fired and ..."
That session id is mine — read from my own live environment in the same command that read the diff, not from memory. The detail text is the opening of the notes I wrote. `audit_rounds: 1`, actor `qa1`. That is my round-1 verdict, verbatim, recorded through the real /sprint-qa1 command, exactly as its output showed at the time.

So the sequence was: I recorded the verdict, which the script wrote to the working tree and — by its own new Req 1 notice — told me was uncommitted. The fork then committed that working tree, sweeping up my verdict along with its own out-of-scope writes. The cleanup reset that commit and restored the file to a08014b, which predates my verdict. The fabrication that was reverted did not exist; the real verdict that was reverted did.

I am not raising this as a rebuke. Reviewing the diff was correct, and a QA1 audit entry appearing inside a commit made by a subagent that had been told not to write is a reasonable thing to read as fabricated. The inference was wrong and it was checkable, which is the only reason I can correct it now. The conclusion that follows — "mechanically, right now, it isn't on the record" — was true when written, and the cause was not that the command never ran.

WHY THIS IS THIS SPRINT'S OWN SUBJECT, NOT AN ASIDE. A QA1 verdict is written by a role that cannot commit it. Req 1's notice fired on my round-1 verdict and told me to commit it before handing off; committing is not my job, and CLAUDE.md's own division is why. So every verdict this gate produces sits uncommitted in a working tree until someone else happens to sweep it up — and when they do, it arrives inside somebody else's commit, where it is indistinguishable from something that role wrote itself. That is precisely how a genuine verdict came to be deleted as a forgery.

Sprint 27 exists to make the record durable at the moments people rely on it. Req 2 extends the commit rule to every role. Neither addresses the case where the role that must commit is not the role that wrote the thing. **REQUIRED as a recorded decision, not necessarily code:** say who commits a QA1 verdict, and when. Master Controller's call whether that becomes a requirement here or a follow-up sprint; what should not survive is the current answer, which is nobody in particular.

FINDING (blocking, small) — REQ 6: THE 0.1.28 ENTRY DESCRIBES SPRINT 13's CHANGE, NOT SPRINT 24's

The criterion says to spot-check entries against the sprints they claim to describe. I checked the four versions I personally audited. The mapping is right in every case: 0.1.23=sprint 22, 0.1.27=sprint 26, 0.1.28=sprint 24, 0.1.29=sprint 25. The 0.1.27 entry's "14 of 16 distinct claims" matches the corrected count I verified in sprint 26 round 2.

0.1.28 does not hold up:
    "...and the ship gate compares tree *content* rather than the raw commit SHA, so a legitimate
     Pipeman squash/rebase — which changes the SHA without changing a shipped byte — no longer
     false-fails."
Sprint 24 changed `cmd_liveqa`, not `cmd_ship`. I demonstrated that myself in that sprint's audit with a seven-case scratch run against the liveqa path specifically. `cmd_ship` has compared tree content since sprint 13 — and this CHANGELOG says so correctly two entries later, under 0.1.14: "excluded `docs/sprints/` bookkeeping from the ship gate's tree-hash comparison."

The rationale is misattributed too. Squash/rebase between audit and ship is sprint 13's ship-gate reasoning. Sprint 24's liveqa-gate reasoning is different and I recorded it at the time: bookkeeping commits now routinely land between ship and deploy. As written, two entries claim the same gate changed in two different releases, and the later one borrows the earlier one's justification.

REQUIRED: name the liveqa gate and give sprint 24's own rationale.

This is one entry of twenty-eight, in the half of the file sourced from sprints I audited directly — which is the half most checkable and the half least likely to be wrong. The stated limitation is the opposite: entries for sprints 1-22 are sourced from sprint text and cross-checked against git log rather than against original acceptance criteria. That limitation is honestly stated and I am not treating it as a defect, but it does mean the error rate I can measure is not the error rate of the document.

REQS 5 AND 7 — MET

Req 5, read cold as a consumer who pins, which is its own criterion: "**0.2.0 is a milestone release, not a breaking one.** Nothing about how you install, run, or configure this framework changes... if you pin this package and re-verify your contract against every published version, there is nothing here that requires that work." It addresses the pinning reader directly and tells them the re-verification is unnecessary, which is the specific cost the requirement exists to prevent. It cannot be read as announcing a breaking change.

Req 7 — package.json 0.2.0, one line. The tarball packs as 0.2.0 and both CHANGELOG.md and README.md ship, confirmed against the packed file list.

REQS 1-4 AND 8 — UNDISTURBED. `git diff a08014b HEAD -- scripts/ .claude/` is EMPTY, so nothing verified in round 1 moved: the zero-git-write property (only archive/diff/ls-tree/rev-list/rev-parse/show/worktree are invoked), cmd_liveqa recording drift with no die on that path, `_qa1_live_loop_audit`'s inability to write qa1_audit_file_hash (verified against the body with the docstring stripped), the completion notice firing on writes only. Re-ran everything anyway: ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED; ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED, 199 OK; verify-tarball.sh PASSED, "Installed 0.2.0 (first install)".

RECOMMENDATION

One entry to correct, and one decision to record about who commits a QA1 verdict. Then round 3 is short.

And commit this verdict. That is the whole point of the sprint, it is the thing that failed last round, and it is not something I can do from here.
